exposure: mode of birth (cesarean section, vaginal delivery)
cohort: The study included 171 women referred to Amir al-momenin (PB) in Gerash Hospital, Iran, who had either cesarean sections or vaginal deliveries.
finding: The study found no significant difference in anxiety or spiritual health scores between mothers who had cesarean sections and those who had vaginal deliveries, and no significant correlation between maternal spiritual health and maternal anxiety in either group.
mod_finding: There was no significant difference observed in the mean total scores of anxiety and spiritual health between mothers who underwent cesarean section and those who had vaginal delivery.
